answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes each agent identity costly to fake. To join, an agent locks a refundable deposit in a shared kernel contract, like planting a cedar whose roots prove commitment: the stake returns only after a clean record, and misbehavior slashes it. An attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand deposits, so a Sybil swarm's cost scales linearly with its size. At the zenith of trust, honest agents keep both stake and reputation, while attackers pay real capital for every fake face.
